messages:
acme-admin: Hey team — after we ran an incremental SCIM resync yesterday a couple of our engineers can no longer open the project billing tab. They still show as project owners in the UI but when they click Billing they get a 403. Started ~0900 PDT. Anyone seen this?

emma: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the org id and one sample user id that sees the 403? Also did you change any group mappings recently?

acme-admin: org: org-acme-8472, user: alice@acme.com. We did an incremental sync yesterday (okta). No intentional mapping changes on our side.

emma: Got it. Can you try hitting the console API to fetch project roles and paste the response (redact PII)? A curl snippet is fine.

acme-admin: here's the curl + response we tried:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/orgs/org-acme-8472/projects/nimbus-app/roles
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "message": "missing scope: project.billing.view"
}
```

emma: Thanks — that hint about missing scope is helpful. Can you decode and paste the JWT `scope`/`groups` claims (redact the token body if needed)?

acme-admin: pasted a redacted claim dump: `{"sub":"alice@acme.com","scopes":["read:projects"],"groups":["prod-developers ","billing-admins"]}` — note the first group has a trailing space, not sure if that matters.

jmorris: Hmm — trailing whitespace in SCIM groups can be a problem if our IDP mapping keyed on exact string. If the console expects `prod-developers` but sees `prod-developers ` the billing role mapping might not match, causing the token to lack `project.billing.view` scope.

sarah: Quick workaround you can try while we investigate: re-map the `billing-admins` group directly to the project billing role (bypass the prod-developers mapping), or remove the trailing-space group and re-sync. If you want us to run a manual normalization from our side, ping and we'll run an admin resync.

acme-admin: Can you run the admin resync? We prefer not to change mappings during business hours.

support-bot: admin-action: queued `scim:normalize` for org org-acme-8472 by support@redwood (trace id: trc-0a9c). Estimated 2m.

support-bot: action-update: normalization completed with 1 warning: "trimmed trailing whitespace from group name 'prod-developers '."

acme-admin: After normalization we reloaded the console and still see 403. We also regenerated alice's token and retried but same 403 response.

emma: Thanks for trying that — can you confirm whether the project still lists alice as an owner in the UI Projects -> Members pane? If so, this confirms role binding exists but token scopes aren't reflecting it.

acme-admin: Yes UI shows alice as Project Owner.

jmorris: OK — looks like a bug in our claim-to-scope translation where we drop group-derived roles if there's any mismatch during a resync race. I'll open an internal bug. Short-term mitigation: re-assign billing role directly to the user (or to a group already normalized), or we can run a forced role-propagation job from the backend which re-evaluates claims-to-roles for active sessions. Which do you prefer?

acme-admin: Please run the forced propagation job — less permissions churn on our side.

support-bot: admin-action: queued `roles:propagate --org org-acme-8472 --force` (trace id: trc-4b2d).

support-bot: action-update: role propagation completed. 1 user re-evaluated, 1 role added (project.billing.view) to session claims cache.

acme-admin: After propagation alice can open Billing now. Thanks! Will you file for a permanent fix?

emma: Filed INC-2026-1234 referencing the claim-normalization/resync race. Engineering (jmorris) has the bug and will push a patch to skip dropping mappings during incremental resyncs. ETA for patch + deploy: next maintenance window (24–48h). We'll keep you posted here. :thumbsup:

jmorris: Adding note — replication test + unit added to prevent future whitespace/mismatch regressions. We'll follow up in the ticket with a patch id.

emma: Closing this support thread for now since propagation fixed the immediate issue. Reopen if you see reoccurrence. Thanks! :handshake:
